newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITIMPEKS SAYS IN TALKS WITH TALLINNA, KREDYT.
newsitem.headline: LITIMPEKS SAYS IN TALKS WITH TALLINNA, KREDYT.

text.p: Lithuania's Litimpeks Bank, which is looking for an investor, said on Friday that it was in talks with Estonia's Tallinna Pank and Poland's Kredyt Bank.
"We have been working with Polish and Estonian banks all week," Gintautas Preidys, the chairman of the bank's board, said at a news conference.
In response to a question, he confirmed that the banks were Estonia's Tallinna Pank and Poland's Kredyt Bank.
Litimpeks, which was reopened last June after being unexpectedly shut by the central bank in December 1995, has faced an uphill struggle to stay on its feet.
The bank has pinned its hopes on a 60 million litas share issue which it will submit to the Securities Comission today.
"It seems we will have one strategic investor who might acquire a 30 to 50 percent stake in our bew issue," Preidys said.
"I don't think that all of the buyers will be foreign investors," he said.
He added that the bank would like to see the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) among its future partners.
"We would like to finish our talks by May 20," he said.
Tallinna Pank earlier said that it was eyeing opportunities in Lithuania and was negotiating with several Lithuanian banks.
Poland's Kredyt Bank last year became the first foregn bank to recieve permission to set up a branch office in Lithuania.
